profiles.line: Gear programme since 2023: subsidises the full cost of requests from students until the year's budget runs out.
Gear programme since 2023: subsidises the full cost of requests from students until the year's budget runs out.
No HQ or closet of their own. Hands product out at Family Week and Atlanta Family Weekend, and refers people to Massachusetts partners.
Counsellors hand out gear codes privately across three offices, half or fully covered. Low volume, roughly one or two orders a year.
BAGLY's Boutique keeps gender-affirming wear in stock with one-on-one sizing help, plus fittings at the annual Trans Youth Summit.
BAGLY's Boutique keeps gender-affirming wear in stock with one-on-one sizing help, plus fittings at the annual Trans Youth Summit.
Free queer closet: clothing, underwear, swimwear, binders, tape and other gender-affirming products.
Free gender-affirming clothing closet people can shop and try on in person. Takes donations of all kinds.
G.E.A.R. programme: request what they hold in stock through an online form, then collect it or have it mailed.
Gender-affirming supports at the Tacoma and Lakewood drop-in centres, open Thursday to Saturday 4-10pm, other times by appointment.
Gender-affirming supports at the Tacoma and Lakewood drop-in centres, open Thursday to Saturday 4-10pm, other times by appointment.
Bins of gender-affirming care items around the space, free for youth to take what they need.
Bins of gender-affirming care items around the space, free for youth to take what they need.
Rainbow Boutique: free gender-affirming clothing for LA County foster youth up to 24. Actively wants extended sizes.
Gear appointments at their office: binders, breast forms, gaffs and packers kept in stock.
Gear appointments at their office: binders, breast forms, gaffs and packers kept in stock.
No closet of their own: hands donated items out on request, and runs an October clothing closet event with the Jim Toy Center.
Mails free gender-affirming, hygiene and period products worldwide to trans people 12 and over facing financial hardship.
Two volunteers stocking and giving out gender-affirming items free across Switzerland. Buys from us to restock.
Low-barrier access for anyone anywhere in Nova Scotia, run from a staffed health clinic. Buys in bulk across separate funding streams.
Sylvia's Closet at their Eugene resource room: free binders, bras, breast forms, tucking and packing underwear. Walk-ins welcome.
Affirming Wardrobes placed with schools, clinics and community orgs across Arizona; since late 2025 running as Reach Pluto from a Tucson church closet.
"On the House" free community closet at their Queen's University drop-in centre, including a Gender Affirming Closet.
Gender-affirming care kits and assistance handed out free through their peer mental-health programme.
Hosts a closet of free gender-affirming clothing and accessories.
30-minute one-on-one appointments to shop their preloved racks with styling support, in a dedicated trans-centric space.
Donation closet at the clinic alongside gender-affirming care, plus outreach across rural Montana including the travelling Trans Closet.
Trans Health Program hands RUBIES gift-card codes to patients one at a time; 100 issued in 2025.
Student-led college Pride Center working toward a gender-affirming closet this year. Nothing standing yet.
Runs gender-affirming clothing swaps and events. On hiatus from receiving and distributing since 2026, relaunching in the new year.
Buys through a renewing discount code and passes items to their local trans community. Renews the code roughly yearly.
Distributes gender-affirming gear to trans kids in Chattanooga (formerly B4CK, Binders for Confident Kids). Has its own space now and sees far more trans girls.
Runs a Gender Affirming Supply Closet as a periodic Saturday event: free supplies plus a swap of new and gently used donated clothing.
Provides gender-affirming items to youth at the centre as the need comes up; also runs an annual Back to School with Pride event.
Wound up their Transgender Whole Healthcare Team in July 2025. Still provides gender-affirming health care, but no community outreach.
Set up a queer closet at their New York clubhouse in 2024, stocked by direct order.
Runs Camp Ga'avah, an LGBTQ+ camp for ages 6-16, with parent and youth groups and monthly programming. No clothing distribution on record.
Hospital gender service for trans and gender-diverse children and teens in Sydney; items reach families through the clinic.
Runs The Closet alongside a youth leadership programme, support groups and the Trans Youth Forum.
Was a donation partner buying at the discount; their programme is no longer running.
Offers donated gender-affirming clothing to local young people in need; received and promoted a box in 2022.
Campus resource centre with free binders on hand for students; asked about adding tucking products.
Free community closet open Friday to Sunday, other days by request: binders, packers, tucking underwear and kits, trans tape, bras and forms.
Free community closet open Friday to Sunday, other days by request: binders, packers, tucking underwear and kits, trans tape, bras and forms.
All their clothing is free, handed out at events that raise very little. Were fundraising for storage bins in 2024.
Project 10's trans programming hands gender gear to Montreal youth as demand comes in, and demand from transfeminine youth is rising.
The Transition Closet serves regular clientele and takes product out to Queer Camp and Fayetteville Pride; stock is listed on their website.
Community closet at their independent trans healthcare centre in Northampton, Massachusetts.
Runs a free store of gender-affirming garments for youth, and would buy more of whatever moves.
Children's mental-health and community services org. What is on the table is fundraising and free webinars, not clothing distribution.
Pride ERG assembling care packages for events (Black Trans Liberation Kitchen, August 2026). Small budget, buys at the partner discount.
Circus arts org that co-hosts the annual Toronto Pride party with us. No distribution of their own.
School board team that shares our Pride party with its Gender Independent Group families. No distribution of their own.
Puts donated items out at their in-person community events for TNBI people to take. Part-time staff, slow inbox.
NHS advocacy, no distribution of their own. Referred us on to Genderswap.
Gender-affirming items closet serving 12 counties in East Central Illinois. Tiny budget, actively wants more transfemme options.
Runs a clothing closet with its own point person; signed up as a donation partner in September 2026.
